intent_en: To illustrate that individuals who do not attend college are concentrated in lower income brackets, supporting the argument that post-secondary training is economically necessary and student debt cancellation is irrelevant for this group.
previous_intent: To demonstrate that individuals who did not attend college are concentrated in lower income brackets, highlighting the economic necessity of post-high school training.
narration_support: Canceling the country's student debt won't help them at all... Right now we have an economy in the 21st century that basically says you're going to need some post -high school training.
chart_support: Bar chart showing income distribution for people who 'DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE', with the highest bars in the lowest income brackets and a sharp decline in higher income brackets, indicating lower earnings for this demographic.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states debt cancellation won't help 'them' (contextually those without college debt) and argues for post-high school training. The chart visualizes the income distribution for 'DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE', showing a heavy concentration in lower income ranges, which supports the economic necessity argument.
